correctness.rationale: For an \(r\)-dimensional message space \(U\), direct counting in \(W=U^\perp\) gives support \(N-p^{n-r}+p^a+s\), where \(a=\dim(W\cap A)\) and \(s\) counts exceptional vectors in \(W\). The dimension formula forces \(a\ge\max(0,m-r)\), so minimizers are exactly those with equality and \(s=0\). For \(r\le m\), quotienting by \(A_0=W\cap A\) turns \(W\) into a graph over the full complement and yields one or \(t\) forbidden graph values depending on whether the distinguished vector lies in \(A_0\). For \(r>m\), the graph domain is an \(h\)-subspace of the complement, and a correction is needed exactly when that domain contains the distinguished direction. Exact exhaustive enumeration for five independent small instances matches every minimum and multiplicity formula.

value.rationale: The primary article presents this as a new infinite nonprojective Griesmer family and emphasizes its optimality and ordinary few-weight structure. Generalized Hamming weights are the standard higher-dimensional refinement of minimum distance, but the hierarchy alone does not measure the multiplicity of extremal subcodes. The closed formulas here classify every minimizer in every dimension and expose how the single exceptional line changes the extremal incidence count through the parameter t. This is a natural structural invariant of the new family and is not recoverable from the ordinary weight distribution.
